key_insight: Charge separation in low-offset organic solar cells is governed by the balance between LE–CT energetic offset, state degeneracy, and Gaussian disorder, which can either hinder or enhance efficiency depending on the regime.
engineering_relevance: Device design can improve performance by tuning molecular energetics and disorder so thermalization and exciton–CT hybridization sustain charge separation even at near-zero or negative offsets.
method: Compared a macroscopic two-state rate model against 3D kinetic Monte Carlo simulations.
Varied the LE–CT offset across the full range and mapped internal quantum efficiency trends.
Tested the impact of Gaussian energetic disorder on charge separation dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the analytical rate model matches kMC across all offsets without disorder, and that disorder changes the efficiency trend with a crossover from mostly harmful at large offsets to beneficial at intermediate and low offsets.
watch_item: The disorder-enhanced efficiency likely depends on material-specific energetic landscapes, so conclusions may not transfer directly without calibrating the offset and disorder parameters for a given blend.
paper_title: Dependence of charge separation efficiency on the exciton-charge transfer offset and Gaussian disorder in organic solar cells
